name: Paid-community pricing and membership benchmarks
demand: Skool’s official Careers page claims 30M+ users, 200,000+ communities and over $1B paid out to creators; the page gives no measurement date or methodology, and those figures do not isolate paid-community operators or benchmark buyers: https://www.skool.com/careers. As supply-side proxies, Check the Course displayed 9,448 listings and 1,252,883 observations on 23 Oct 2026: https://checkthecourse.com/. Skool Inspector displayed 11,785 communities and 6,034 subscription communities in its 22 Oct 2026 update: https://skoolinspector.evyai.com/stats. Search volume, installs, unique paid-operator count and willingness to pay for an independent benchmark are unverified.
prices: Public reports from Check the Course and CommunityRank have no subscription price displayed; their subscription pricing is unverified: https://checkthecourse.com/reports https://community-rank.com/report. Skool Analytics explicitly says it is free with no card: https://www.skoolanalytics.com/. Skool Stats was listed at $149/month for 200 email enrichments in an Oct 2026 pricing review; this is an asking price for adjacent lead intelligence, not verified sales or a benchmark subscription: https://toolradar.com/tools/skool-stats/pricing. Skoolgrades Pro displays $19/month against a $39 price, but it is owner-side analytics rather than a cross-market benchmark: https://www.skoolgrades.com/get-pro. Skool’s own plans are $9/month and $99/month; its analytics announcement describes analytics for an owner’s community, not a standalone market benchmark: https://www.skool.com/pricing https://www.skool.com/explore-3828/skool-news-36-analytics-is-live.
copy_speed: Competition is already close to the proposed product. Check the Course tracks prices and member counts with history; its page showed about 10 weeks of history on 23 Oct 2026: https://checkthecourse.com/. Skool Inspector advertises daily market statistics, Skool Analytics records daily snapshots, and CommunityRank publishes weekly Skool/Whop rankings: https://skoolinspector.evyai.com/stats https://www.skoolanalytics.com/ https://community-rank.com/. A Skoolgrades participation benchmark page is dated 29 Jul 2026: https://www.skoolgrades.com/published/skool-community-benchmarks. Skool Stats was listed in a directory on 17 Oct 2026, but that is not proof of its launch date: https://www.purshology.com/directory/skool-stats/. Exact launch dates for most of these products are unverified.
platform_risk: Critical for a dataset gathered from platform pages. Skool’s terms prohibit commercial compilation of directories from its displayed content and prohibit manual or automated scraping, copying or monitoring: https://www.skool.com/legal?t=terms. Whop’s terms, last updated 9 Oct 2026, prohibit automated monitoring and scraping without written consent: https://whop.com/tos/. Skool’s documented Zapier integration is Pro-only and lists four member-related triggers/actions, not a general public data feed: https://help.skool.com/article/56-zapier-integration. A scraping-led version therefore has material terms and continuity risk; permissioned submissions, a license or written platform authorization would be needed for a defensible data source.
defensible_asset: Historical data is a qualifying moat type in principle, but the proposed public price/member-count dataset is already replicated by several services, including free-to-access reports and directories: https://checkthecourse.com/reports https://community-rank.com/report https://skoolinspector.evyai.com/stats. Price multiplied by public membership is only an upper-bound estimate, not verified revenue; Check the Course explicitly explains that it omits trials, discounts, churn, refunds and other factors: https://checkthecourse.com/. No network effect or customer switching cost is evidenced. A stronger moat would require unique, permissioned longitudinal data such as verified paid membership, retention or owner-submitted outcomes.
build_effort: Estimated high for broad multi-platform coverage, lower for a narrow opt-in pilot. The product needs permissioned data acquisition, source and observation dates, consistent niche and billing-period normalization, history, quality checks and report generation; existing trackers show that daily or weekly updates are technically feasible, but do not establish their staffing or costs: https://checkthecourse.com/reports/skool-pricing-benchmarks https://www.skoolanalytics.com/ https://community-rank.com/. No build duration or operating cost is verified.
channel: Use owned SEO pages and free tools, contextual search ads, and inbound or warm partnerships/integrations backed by written data permission; no cold email, SMS, DM or calls. For UK advertising, the ICO says contextual advertising can more readily meet PECR/UK GDPR requirements, while storage/access technologies for online advertising require consent: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/how-do-the-rules-apply-to-online-advertising/. Keep signup marketing opt-in; verify local ad and privacy requirements before targeting each other country.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. This is a build lead with no operating business or measured founder workload, so the <=5 h/week constraint is not evidenced.
automation_reason: 55% is my estimate for a permissioned or opt-in data model, not a measured result. Agents could normalize and validate submissions, update charts, draft SEO pages, handle billing/admin and triage routine support. The owner would still need to secure data rights, review anomalies and make product decisions. Existing services demonstrate recurring updates, but provide no evidence of their actual automation share or founder hours: https://checkthecourse.com/ https://www.skoolanalytics.com/ https://community-rank.com/.
moat_assessment: Conditional and currently weak. Compiled historical data fits the required moat category on paper, but free competitors already publish overlapping data, and the platform terms make the proposed collection route problematic. Treat the moat as unproven unless a permissioned source yields unique data that users cannot easily reproduce. No network effect or switching costs are verified: https://checkthecourse.com/ https://www.skoolgrades.com/published/skool-community-benchmarks https://www.skool.com/legal?t=terms https://whop.com/tos/.
desk_test: Within one workday, make a one-page, clearly labeled pilot offer for one narrow operator segment, using only operator-submitted or otherwise authorized sample data. Check relevant search queries, then use contextual search ads to measure opt-ins or paid pilot reservations; do not use tracking technologies without required consent or send unsolicited messages. Record any paid reservations separately from expressions of interest. UK ad and tracking guidance: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/how-do-the-rules-apply-to-online-advertising/.
red_flags: No verified customer payments, revenue, churn, owner hours or willingness to pay for this proposed service. Competitor list prices are offers, not revenue proof. The platform’s own $1B payout claim is about Skool creators overall, not this product: https://www.skool.com/careers. Public membership multiplied by list price can misstate actual earnings: https://checkthecourse.com/. The largest execution risk is acquiring and retaining lawful data rights while competing against already available benchmark products.
